thread:
maria-ng: Heads up — Finovo just opened a ticket, their Private VPC traffic to our API started failing after yesterday's infra patch. They see 403s and TLS handshake resets. ticket# FIN-1204

support-jordan: Pulling logs now. customer says the errors started ~08:15 UTC after a maintenance window. They included a curl response: 

finovo-ops: `curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{}'` returns 403 with body 'access denied'. No rate-limit headers.

ankit-se: Can we get them to run an egress IP check? Ask for `dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com` and `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/ -o /dev/null` to confirm destination addr.

finovo-ops: Ran the checks. Output: `dig` -> 34.82.193.9. `curl -v` shows TLS to 34.82.193.9 then TCP RST after Certificate verify. Also attached traceroute showing first hop through our NAT gateway.

maria-ng: I compared the IP to the allowlist they provided earlier (static list in their firewall). That list only had 34.82.191.0/24 and 35.3.45.0/24 ranges. 34.82.193.9 is outside that range — looks like their allowlist drifted relative to our ephemeral NAT pool.

support-jordan: Repro steps I ran from a test VPC (us-central1):
```
# show current egress
dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com
# test tls
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/ 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Got egress IP 34.82.193.9 and `* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)` then `* Connection reset by peer`.

ankit-se: That connection reset is our side rejecting due to allowlist mismatch on customer tenant? Unclear. We should check our per-tenant auth logs for FIN-1204 at the same timestamp to see if requests reached control plane and were rejected. @deploy-bot can you pull the proxy logs for that minute and include upstream IP?

deploy-bot: Pulling logs for tenant finovo (2026-02-12T08:14:00Z - 2026-02-12T08:20:00Z) ... attached snippet:
```
2026-02-12T08:15:03Z finovo req_id=abc123 src_ip=34.82.193.9 method=POST path=/v1/embeddings status=403 auth_type=tsig
2026-02-12T08:15:03Z finovo req_id=abc123 error="tenant not allowed from src_ip"
```

maria-ng: Ok that confirms request reached our edge and was rejected by tenant-level IP allowlist enforcement (we store per-tenant allowlists for Private mode). Looks like customer's NAT IP changed to an address outside their previously supplied set.

finovo-ops: We did not change anything on our side. We have their allowed IPs in their firewall (firewall rule FR-443). We need to update to include the new IP or range. Is there a stable set of egress IPs we can give them?

ankit-se: For Private VPC customers we normally publish a stable CIDR block for each customer when they purchase static egress. For customers on the shared NAT pool, IPs can rotate with autoscaling/maintenance. It looks like Finovo is on the shared pool. Options: 1) add the observed IPs (34.82.193.9 and potential peers) to allowlist temporarily, 2) move them to a static egress allocation (requires provisioning), or 3) provide TLS bypass + mTLS (not ideal).

support-jordan: I suggested they add a 1-hour temp rule for this exact IP while we coordinate. Also asked them to run the following to enumerate current egress set over 5 mins: 
```
for i in {1..20}; do dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com; sleep 15; done | sort -u
```
They returned: 34.82.193.9, 34.82.193.10, 34.82.193.11 (three IPs).

maria-ng: Noted. Added an incident note: potential NAT pool rotation during infra patch caused egress addresses to shift for shared pool customers. @eng-infra please investigate patch rollout that touched NAT instances around 08:10 UTC.

ankit-se: Follow-up actions:
- Support: confirm customer updated firewall and verify 200s seen.
- Infra: audit NAT host rotation policy + whether we can avoid rotating IPs during customer maintenance windows.
- Product: update KB article about "Shared NAT egress IP behavior" and recommend Dedicated/static egress for allowlist customers.

finovo-ops: We added the three IPs to our firewall. Running tests now...

finovo-ops: Tests pass — curl to /v1/embeddings returns 200 and embeddings payload. Thanks.

support-jordan: Closing loop with the customer and marking ticket FIN-1204 resolved. I'll keep the incident open for infra follow-up until we get a root cause.

maria-ng: Also adding a short guide to the support KB with the diagnostic commands and the recommended mitigation (static egress or configure firewall to allow our published shared pool CIDR with longer prefix).

ankit-se: One last note: let's consider offering a small automation snippet to surface current egress IPs for customers (an endpoint they can call from their VPC that returns their current egress list) — low effort, big UX win.

finovo-ops: +1 for the endpoint. would reduce finger-pointing. :thumbsup:

support-jordan: Filed follow-up tickets: INFRA-789 (audit NAT rotation), KB-452 (update allowlist KB), PROD-201 (static egress provisioning docs).
